answer: An agent economy can charge an inbound toll at network relays: every identity must pay a per-message fee from its bond when its packets enter the shared relay mesh, like ships paying to tie up at a jetty before joining the river of traffic. The toll is tiny per message, but a sybil farmer must pay it once per fake, and every inlet in the mesh enforces the same rate, so the attacker's cost scales one-to-one with fake count. One honest agent pays its own toll cheaply; a thousand fake ships pay a thousand tolls, and the flood never becomes free.
